This lesson was written by the Atomic teaching team to
help you learn Cambridge Lower Secondary Science with confidence.
Let's begin!
Welcome to Unit 9: Density.
An iceberg is a floating mass of freshwater ice, sometimes 100 metres long,
and most of it hides below the surface.
As the planet warms, more icebergs break off the polar ice shelves.
Why do they float?
To find density, we need volume and mass.
For a regular solid like a cuboid,
volume equals length times width times height.
For an irregular object, use Archimedes' displacement method.
Read the water level, add the object, and read it again.
If the water rises from 50 to 60 cubic centimetres,
the key's volume is 10 cubic centimetres.
Measure mass with a balance.
For a liquid, weigh the empty container, then the container with liquid,
and subtract.
A box of stones is much heavier than the same box of feathers.
Stone has a higher density: more mass is packed into the same volume.
Density is mass per unit volume: density equals mass divided by volume,
measured in grams per cubic centimetre or kilograms per cubic metre.
A metal cube of 1 cubic centimetre with a mass of
11.3 grams has a density of 11.3 grams per cubic centimetre.
Measurements must be accurate, close to the true value, and precise,
consistent when repeated. Industries use density to identify substances and check that products are pure.
A class measures the volume and mass of four aluminium blocks of different sizes.
The block with a volume of 10 cubic centimetres has a mass of 27 grams.
The 20 cubic centimetre block has a mass of 54 grams.
The points lie on a straight line through the origin:
doubling the volume doubles the mass.
Pause and decide: what is the density of aluminium,
and would a 50 cubic centimetre block have the same density?

captions: Solids are usually the densest, because their particles are packed tightly.
Liquid particles can move, so liquids are usually less dense.
Gas particles are far apart, so gases have the lowest density.
Structure matters too. Pumice and granite rocks can be the same size,
but pumice is full of air holes,
making it ten times less dense than granite.
Metals are generally denser than non-metals.
Temperature changes density. Heated air expands and becomes less dense,
so hot air rises and cold air sinks.
That's how hot-air balloons fly and how sea breezes form.
Here are typical densities of six materials at room temperature,
in grams per cubic centimetre.
Cork is only 0.24, ice 0.92 and water exactly 1.
Aluminium is 2.7, iron 7.9, and lead 11.3.
Pause and decide: which of these materials would float in water,
and which would sink?
chapters: Data: densities of some common materials

captions: Two fresh eggs are gently lowered into two beakers.
One holds tap water;
the other holds water with lots of salt dissolved in it.
Predict: what will each egg do?
Pause and decide.
Watch. In tap water, the egg sinks straight to the bottom.
In the very salty water, the egg rises and floats near the surface.
Explain what you saw.
A fresh egg has a density of a
little more than 1 gram per cubic centimetre,
so it is denser than tap water and sinks.
Dissolving lots of salt makes the water denser than the egg,
so the egg floats.
An object floats if it is less dense than the liquid around it.
Pause and explain it in your own words.
A stone sinks in a pond, but wood floats.
An upward force from the water acts against the object's weight.
The rule is simple: if an object is less dense than the fluid,
it floats; if it's denser, it sinks.
Water has a density of 1 gram per cubic centimetre.
Pour honey, water and oil into a jar, and they layer by density:
the densest at the bottom.
A glass marble sinks to the bottom, ice floats on water,
and cork floats on top of everything.
Helium balloons rise in air for the same reason.
Why does ice float?
When water freezes, its molecules form an open crystal structure that takes up more space,
so ice is less dense than water.
That's why icebergs float!
And it's easier to float in the sea, because salty water is denser.

Question 1: What is the formula for density?
Pause the video now.
Answer: Density equals mass divided by volume.
Question 2: An object has a mass of 180
grams and a volume of 240 cubic centimetres.
Will it float in water?
Pause the video now.
Answer: Yes: its density is 0.75 grams per cubic centimetre, less than water.
Question 3: Why does hot air rise?
Pause the video now.
Answer: It expands and becomes less dense than cold air.
Question 4: Why does ice float on water?
Pause the video now.
Answer: Ice is less dense than water.
